item.title: Odd Lots: Weber’s Vision for an Affordability Agenda (Podcast)
item.description: The most important word in politics right now is affordability. It was a winning issue in the midterms for Democrats, and one of the reasons why people across Europe are out in the streets protesting: Food, housing, and energy are getting more expensive by the day. During the height of the pandemic, we talked a lot about inflation with Isabella Weber, and her on what governments can do to make life more affordable has evolved into a book called Anti-Fascist Economics: In Defense of Affordability
item.dc:creator: Joe Weisenthal and Tracy Alloway

item.title: Dubai Stocks Erase Wartime Losses to Become a Top Gulf Performer
item.description: Dubai stocks have erased all losses since the Iran war began, transforming from the Gulf’s biggest laggard into one of its best performers, driven by government support and resilient economic activity.
item.dc:creator: Farah Elbahrawy and Laura Gardner Cuesta

item.title: Euro Set for Biggest Annual Drop Against Yuan in Two Decades
item.description: The euro is set for its biggest annual slide against the yuan in two decades, with European officials calling on China to let its currency strengthen further to curb surging imports.
item.dc:creator: Ran Li

item.title: US Futures Rally as Tech Rebound Gains Momentum: Markets Wrap
item.description: US stocks are set to rally strongly when trade resumes after Thanksgiving, with a rebound in the artificial intelligence trade poised to round out a week of sharp swings on a positive note.
item.dc:creator: Andre Janse van Vuuren and Macarena Muñoz

item.title: China Bank Bond Spreads Head for Biggest Jump in Over Two Years
item.description: Chinese bank bond spreads are heading for their biggest monthly increase since September 2024, as debt strain at a major state-owned conglomerate ripples through the broader credit market.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News

item.title: Ghana Buys Back $1.1 Billion Domestic Bonds to Boost Confidence
item.description: Ghana redeemed a four-year domestic bond three months ahead of maturity, as the government sought to bolster investor confidence in an economy recovering from a debt restructuring.
item.dc:creator: Moses Mozart Dzawu

item.title: US Investors Will Have to Chase Rally: Market Analysis
item.description: Guy Johnson, Tom Mackenzie and Mark Cudmore break down today's key themes for analysts and investors on "Bloomberg: The Opening Trade." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hong Kong Dollar Hits Six-Month High as Funding Costs Climb
item.description: The Hong Kong dollar extended its rally to a six-month high, propelled by surging local borrowing costs and demand from investors snapping up the city’s equities amid a rally in Chinese stocks.
item.dc:creator: Jiefei Liu

item.title: Qatar’s LNG Export Push Provides Lifeline to South Asian Buyers
item.description: Qatar’s efforts to export more liquefied natural gas through the Strait of Hormuz are already saving money for South Asia’s cash-strapped importers of the super-chilled fuel.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Stapczynski

item.title: US Stocks Set to Bounce as Risk Appetite Returns After Holiday
item.description: US stocks are poised to rebound, with risk appetite returning after a selloff that brought the Nasdaq 100 index to the brink of a bear market.

item.title: Kuwait Says Iranian Drone Strike Kills Two as Houthi Attack Hits Jazan Refinery
item.description: Horizons Middle East & Africa is your daily spotlight on one of the world's fastest-growing regions. All that and more, as you head to the office in the Gulf, pause for lunch in Hong Kong, or start your day in London or Johannesburg. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Tobacco Climbs on Potential Imperial Brands Takeover
item.description: Japan Tobacco Inc. shares rose on news that it is exploring a potential takeover of Imperial Brands Plc with Altria Group Inc., a move that could help the Japanese cigarette maker fill a large earnings hole left by the recent seizure of its Russian assets.
item.dc:creator: Mia Glass and Kentaro Tsutsumi

item.title: Watch Stockpiling in Oil Markets in 2027: Energy Aspects
item.description: Oil stockpiling will be important factor for the next couple of years, potentially tightening the market and aiding prices even with a projected global surplus, according to Energy Aspects Ltd. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pay Policy at South Africa’s Momentum Passes With 51% Support
item.description: Shareholders in Momentum Group Ltd. narrowly approved the South African insurer’s remuneration policy as new rules give investors in the nation’s firms greater say over compensation.

item.title: Indonesia Palm Oil Tenders Stall on Weak Demand and Tight Supply
item.description: Indonesia’s state-linked palm oil tenders failed to produce a single deal in the past week as tight supply and weak overseas demand kept buyers and sellers far apart on price.

item.title: Indonesia Arrests Three Over Trades in Stock Scrutinized by MSCI
item.description: Indonesian police said Friday they had arrested three people over alleged manipulation of shares of PT Dian Swastatika Sentosa, one of three companies tied to regulatory sanctions announced last month after MSCI Inc. proposed a two-step downgrade of Indonesia’s market status.
